info.name: CBA Platform API — Complete Reference (v2)
info.description:
# Core Banking Application (CBA) API Reference

## Platform Overview
The CBA platform is a production-grade, multi-tenanted core banking system modelled on Apache Fineract / Mifos X conventions. It provides a secure, RESTful API for building banking applications including backoffice portals, customer mobile apps, and third-party integrations via Open Banking (FAPI 2.0).

## Base URL
- **Development**: http://localhost:8080
- **Staging**: https://api-staging.cba.com
- **Production**: https://api.cba.com

## Authentication
All API requests require authentication. The CBA platform uses OAuth2 / OpenID Connect via Keycloak.

### Obtaining a Token
```
POST http://localhost:8180/realms/cba/protocol/openid-connect/token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

client_id=cba-web&grant_type=password&username=admin@cba.com&password=Admin@123
```

Include the returned `access_token` in every request:
```
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
```

### Demo Credentials
| Role | Username | Password |
|------|----------|---------|
| Admin | admin@cba.com | Admin@123 |
| Teller | teller@cba.com | Teller@123 |
| Customer | customer@cba.com | Customer@123 |

## Multi-Tenancy
Every request must include the tenant header:
```
X-Tenant-ID: default
```
Available tenants: `default` (USD), `cba-kenya` (KES), `cba-ghana` (GHS)

## Response Envelope
All responses use the standard CBA envelope:
```json
{
  "data": { ... },
  "meta": { "page": 0, "size": 20, "total": 150 },
  "errors": []
}
```

## Error Format
```json
{
  "data": null,
  "meta": {},
  "errors": [{ "code": "ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND", "message": "Account 123 not found", "field": null }]
}
```

## General Options
- `?page=0&size=20` — Pagination
- `?sort=createdAt,desc` — Sorting
- `?fields=id,name` — Field restriction (where supported)

## HTTP Status Codes
| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 200 | Success |
| 201 | Created |
| 400 | Validation error / bad request |
| 401 | Unauthenticated |
| 403 | Unauthorized (insufficient role) |
| 404 | Resource not found |
| 409 | Conflict (duplicate resource) |
| 500 | Server error |

## Code Samples
Every request includes samples in: **cURL, JavaScript (fetch), Python (requests), Java (OkHttp), C# (HttpClient), PHP (cURL), Go (net/http), Ruby (Net::HTTP)**

## Collection Variables
Set these in Postman before making requests:
| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| base_url | http://localhost:8080 | API base URL |
| access_token | (paste JWT) | Keycloak access token |
| tenant_id | default | Active tenant |

item.name: 00 · Authentication
item.description:
## Authentication Overview

The CBA platform supports OAuth2 Resource Owner Password Credentials Grant via **Keycloak 23+**.

### How It Works
1. POST credentials to Keycloak token endpoint
2. Receive `access_token` (JWT, valid 300s) and `refresh_token`
3. Include `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` on every API request
4. Refresh before expiry using the refresh token

### FAPI 2.0 (Open Banking)
For Open Banking (AISP/PISP/CBPII) endpoints, the platform supports FAPI 2.0 with PAR + DPoP + PKCE. Standard backoffice endpoints use regular Bearer tokens.

### RBAC Roles
| Role | Description |
|------|-------------|
| ADMIN | Full platform access |
| TELLER | Customer/account/cash operations |
| CUSTOMER | Own accounts only (self-service) |
| API_CLIENT | Third-party TPP Open Banking access |

        'username' => 'admin@cba.com',
        'password' => 'Admin@123'

    CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true

item.name: 01 · Customers
item.description:
## Customer Module

Manages customer KYC onboarding, profile management, lifecycle commands, staff assignment, and inter-branch transfer. Full Mifos parity added in Session 49.

### Status Flow (7 States)
```
PENDING_KYC → ACTIVE → SUSPENDED → CLOSED
PENDING_KYC → REJECTED  (undoable via undoRejection)
PENDING_KYC → WITHDRAWN  (undoable via undoWithdrawal)
ACTIVE → TRANSFER_IN_PROGRESS → ACTIVE (accepted/rejected/withdrawn)
```

### Key Rules
- All PII (name, email, phone, national ID) is encrypted at field level (AES-256)
- Lifecycle fields (dates, reasons, staffId, officeId, transfer) are set by service commands only
- Only PENDING_KYC customers can be deleted; others must be closed first
- KYC status changes are immutably logged in the audit trail
- `?command=` pattern (Mifos convention): single POST endpoint dispatches 14 lifecycle transitions

### Required Role
- Read: ADMIN, TELLER
- Write (profile): ADMIN
- Commands: ADMIN (lifecycle), ADMIN/TELLER (staff assignment)

request.description:
Mifos command pattern — dispatches lifecycle transitions via `?command=` query parameter. Returns the updated Customer object.

### Available Commands

| Command | From State | To State | Payload |
|---------|-----------|----------|---------|
| `activate` | PENDING_KYC | ACTIVE | — |
| `reject` | PENDING_KYC | REJECTED | `reason` (opt) |
| `withdraw` | PENDING_KYC, ACTIVE | WITHDRAWN | `reason` (opt) |
| `reactivate` | SUSPENDED | ACTIVE | — |
| `undoRejection` | REJECTED | PENDING_KYC | — |
| `undoWithdrawal` | WITHDRAWN | PENDING_KYC | — |
| `suspend` | ACTIVE | SUSPENDED | `reason` (opt) |
| `close` | ACTIVE, SUSPENDED | CLOSED | `reason` (opt) |
| `assignStaff` | any non-CLOSED | (unchanged) | `staffId` (UUID, required) |
| `unassignStaff` | any non-CLOSED | (unchanged) | — |
| `proposeTransfer` | ACTIVE | TRANSFER_IN_PROGRESS | `destinationOfficeId` (required), `transferDate` (opt), `transferNote` (opt) |
| `acceptTransfer` | TRANSFER_IN_PROGRESS | ACTIVE | — |
| `rejectTransfer` | TRANSFER_IN_PROGRESS | ACTIVE | — |
| `withdrawTransfer` | TRANSFER_IN_PROGRESS | ACTIVE | — |

package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "net/http"
    "strings"
    "io/ioutil"
)

func customerCommand(customerID, command, body string) {
    req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST",
        fmt.Sprintf("{{base_url}}/api/v1/customers/%s?command=%s", customerID, command),
        strings.NewReader(body))
    req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer {{access_token}}")
    req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
    req.Header.Set("X-Tenant-ID", "{{tenant_id}}")
    resp, _ := new(http.Client).Do(req)
    defer resp.Body.Close()
    b, _ := ioutil.ReadAll(resp.Body)
    fmt.Println(string(b))
}

func main() {
    customerCommand("{{customerId}}", "activate", "{}")
    customerCommand("{{customerId}}", "reject", "{\"reason\":\"Insufficient documentation\"}")
    customerCommand("{{customerId}}", "assignStaff", "{\"staffId\":\"uuid-of-staff\"}")
}

require 'net/http'
require 'json'

def customer_command(customer_id, command, payload = {})
  uri = URI("{{base_url}}/api/v1/customers/#{customer_id}")
  uri.query = URI.encode_www_form(command: command)
  http = Net::HTTP.new(uri.host, uri.port)
  req = Net::HTTP::Post.new(uri)
  req['Authorization'] = 'Bearer {{access_token}}'
  req['Content-Type'] = 'application/json'
  req['X-Tenant-ID'] = '{{tenant_id}}'
  req.body = payload.to_json
  http.request(req).body
end

item.description:
## Loan Module

Full loan lifecycle management: origination → disbursement → repayment → collections → closure.

### Status Flow
```
SUBMITTED → UNDER_REVIEW → APPROVED → DISBURSED → ACTIVE → CLOSED_OBLIGATIONS_MET
```
Sub-states: `IN_ARREARS`
Terminal states: `WRITTEN_OFF`, `CLOSED_OBLIGATIONS_MET`

### EMI Formula
```
EMI = P × r × (1+r)^n / ((1+r)^n - 1)
Where: P = principal, r = monthly rate, n = term months
```

### Repayment Types
| Type | Description |
|------|-------------|
| ANNUITY | Equal installments (default) |
| FLAT | Fixed principal + declining interest |
| DECLINING_BALANCE | Interest on outstanding balance |

### Key Rules
- Loan products define the allowed ranges; individual loans must be within those ranges
- Repayment schedule generated on approval, locked on disbursement
- Arrears classification runs nightly (CoB job)

item.name: 04 · Payments & Transfers
item.description:
## Payment Module

Internal account-to-account transfers, external payments (SWIFT/SEPA stubs), standing orders, and bill payments.

### Payment States
```
PENDING → PROCESSING → COMPLETED
                    → FAILED → REVERSED
```

### Double-Entry Ledger
Every transfer atomically debits the source and credits the destination. Both accounts must be locked (`SELECT FOR UPDATE`) before any balance modification.

### Cross-Currency Transfers
When source and destination accounts hold different currencies, the `ExchangeRateService` is invoked automatically. Both accounts are updated in their own currency. The payment record stores `sourceCurrency`, `destinationCurrency`, `exchangeRateUsed`, and `isCrossCurrency=true`.

### Payment Application Logic (Fineract Convention)
Loan repayments are applied in this order:
1. Outstanding fees and penalties
2. Interest due
3. Principal due

item.description:
## Product Module

Loan products and deposit products define the configuration templates that individual loans and accounts are created from.

### Loan Products
Configure: principal range, interest rate range, term range, repayment type, fees, and compounding frequency.

### Deposit Products
Configure: account type (SAVINGS/CHECKING/FIXED_DEPOSIT), minimum balance, interest rate, and compounding frequency.

### Validation Rules
- `minPrincipal ≤ maxPrincipal`
- `minInterestRate ≤ defaultInterestRate ≤ maxInterestRate`
- `minTermMonths ≤ maxTermMonths`

### Required Role
- Read: All authenticated roles
- Write: ADMIN only

item.name: 06 · Teller / Cash Management
item.description:
## Teller / Cash Management Module

Full Mifos-style teller desk, cashier allocation, and session-based cash operations.

### Status Flow
**Teller Desk**: `INACTIVE → ACTIVE → CLOSED`
**Session**: `OPEN → CLOSED`

### Session Lifecycle
1. Admin creates teller desk (`POST /tellers`)
2. Admin activates desk (`POST /tellers/{id}/activate`)
3. Admin assigns cashier to desk (`POST /tellers/{id}/cashiers`)
4. Cashier opens daily session with opening float (`POST /tellers/{id}/cashiers/{cId}/sessions`)
5. Cashier records cash-in / cash-out transactions throughout the day
6. End of day: cashier closes session with physical cash count

### Settlement Formula
```
closing_balance = opening_balance + Σ(CASH_IN) - Σ(CASH_OUT)
difference = actual_cash - closing_balance
```
A positive `difference` means cash surplus; negative means shortage.

### Constraint
Only one open session per cashier per calendar day (enforced at DB level with UNIQUE constraint).

### Account Linking
Cash transactions can optionally link to a customer account. When `accountId` is provided, the account balance is updated atomically and an immutable transaction ledger entry is created.

### Base Path
All Open Banking endpoints use `/open-banking/v3.1/` prefix.

### Roles
| Role | Description |
|------|-------------|
| AISP | Account Information Service Provider — read account/transaction data |
| PISP | Payment Initiation Service Provider — initiate domestic payments |
| CBPII | Card-Based Payment Instrument Issuer — funds confirmation |

### Consent Flow
```
POST /consents → AWAITING_AUTHORISATION
PUT /consents/{id}/authorise → AUTHORISED
(use for AISP/PISP/CBPII operations)
DELETE /consents/{id} → REVOKED
```

### Required Scopes
| Scope | Operations Allowed |
|-------|-------------------|
| `accounts` | AISP: read accounts, balances, transactions |
| `payments` | PISP: initiate domestic payments |
| `fundsconfirmation` | CBPII: check available funds |

### Consent Validation
Before every PISP or CBPII call, the platform validates:
1. Consent status = AUTHORISED
2. Required scope is present
3. Consent has not expired

item.name: 08 · Tenants & Exchange Rates
item.description:
Tenant management and multi-currency exchange rates.

## Exchange Rate Module

The CBA platform supports multi-currency deployment. Each tenant has a configured base currency (ISO 4217).

### Available Tenants
| Tenant | Base Currency |
|--------|--------------|
| default | USD |
| cba-kenya | KES |
| cba-ghana | GHS |

### Exchange Rate Convention
`1 fromCurrency = rate toCurrency` — e.g., USD/KES = 135.50 means 1 USD buys 135.50 KES.

### Auto-Inverse
When you set the USD→KES rate, the KES→USD rate is automatically calculated and stored. You never need to set both directions.

### Rate Precision
Rates are stored to 8 decimal places (`NUMERIC(19,8)`) for accuracy on exotic currency pairs.

### Pre-configured Rates (Demo)
USD↔KES, USD↔GHS, KES↔GHS, USD↔EUR, USD↔GBP

item.name: 09 · Batch API
item.description:
## Batch API

Execute multiple API operations in a single HTTP request. Supports dependent requests and atomic transactions.

### Key Features
- **Dependent requests**: Reference output from a prior request using JSON Path (`$.id`)
- **Atomic execution**: Add `?enclosingTransaction=true` to roll back all on any failure
- **Ordering**: Requests are executed in `requestId` order

### Common Use Cases
- Create customer → open account → apply for loan (onboarding workflow)
- Bulk account queries for a customer
- Batch repayment recording

### Request Object Fields
| Field | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|

item.description:
## Audit Log Module

An immutable, append-only log of every state-changing operation in the platform.

### Key Rules
- **Never updated or deleted** — audit records are permanent
- **REQUIRES_NEW transaction** — audit is persisted even if the main transaction rolls back
- **Minimum retention**: 10 years (compliance requirement)
- **PII masked** in log entries — account numbers shown as `****1234`

### Fields
| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| entityType | e.g., Customer, Account, Loan |
| entityId | UUID of the affected record |
| action | e.g., CREATE, UPDATE, APPROVE, DISBURSE |
| changedBy | User/system that triggered the change |
| oldValues | JSONB snapshot before change |
| newValues | JSONB snapshot after change |
| changedAt | Timestamp (TIMESTAMPTZ) |
| ipAddress | Request origin IP |

item.name: Webhook Management

request.description:
Register a webhook endpoint. Secret returned exactly once — use it to verify X-CBA-Signature on incoming deliveries. Empty events array subscribes to all event types.

Signature verification: compute HMAC-SHA256(payload, secret) and compare with X-CBA-Signature header value (format: sha256={hex}). Use constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks.

Supported events: AUTHORIZATION.APPROVED, AUTHORIZATION.DECLINED, AUTHORIZATION.REVERSED, CARD.ISSUED, CARD.ACTIVATED, CARD.BLOCKED, CARD.UNBLOCKED, CARD.EXPIRED, CARD.PIN_CHANGED, CARD.LIMIT_CHANGED, FRAUD.RULE_TRIGGERED, FRAUD.CARD_STEP_UP, FRAUD.CARD_DECLINED_HIGH_RISK, DISPUTE.RAISED, DISPUTE.RESOLVED

API_KEY or ADMIN required.
